rationale: Both skeptics independently converge on the decisive fact: the two missing theorems share one hard kernel. Route 1's only surviving path through T5 (the conjugated fold, #1158 §3) requires a transport theorem preserving owner and chronology — whole-line first-match properties, i.e. exactly Route 2's selector burden (K3-skeptic Cut 3). Route 2's WLCS requires slope-global earlier-owner exclusion, a K-adjudicated domain, distinct-slope fibers, and a residual fence — SEM-QBC conditions (3)/(4), (FIB), and the all-Z_BC fence in different clothes (S/A/E-skeptic Cut 2; obstruction map: the d1 shift "binds BOTH"). Funding either pure route means re-deriving the other's kernel in incompatible notation. The routes genuinely diverge only at T5 (endpoint realization: no cheap probe, dies late, 12–18 packets exposed) versus L5 (varying-core disjointness: collision falsifier pre-registered by its own author). Bankability points opposite ways — K3 flows through our living #1152 with two exact external replays; S/A/E sits on Scott's unmerged 40-commit branch with N1163 §7 pre-registering the forest compiler as his own next move, plus the m2-collision precedent — so neither divergent half should be funded before the probes run. Three probes costing under 3 packets total (P3 reserve arithmetic on the 31-slot/134944 mismatch; the d1=67473 boundary-record K-adapter test; the #1160-line P_BC rejection regression) are jointly decisive, and two of the three serve both routes. Build the shared spine — executable P_Q/P_BC as typed parsed relations, soundness, the K-adapter, slope-global Q exclusion — run the probes concurrently, and let outcomes select the divergent half. Under every probe outcome the spine is consumed verbatim by the winner; under a pure-route commitment, a T5 late death or an L1 stranding wastes the larger share.

K3's three probes are cheap and real but none touches T5, the hardest step — death arrives after 9-12 sunk packets. S/A/E's P3 (integer-only reserve replay) kills or reprices the route at lemma one for under one packet; P1 (smallest selector collision) is pre-registered in the source itself; P2 controls are explicit objects. Cheaper, earlier, more decisive kill sequence.
